title: Read and write through git's streaming plumbing instead of one process per verb
description:
internal/runstate/git.go:152 commitWithFile writes every durable record as: hash-object, read-tree, update-index, write-tree, commit-tree, then push and rev-parse. Seven processes per record, ~90 records per fixture epic.

Measured: 21.6ms to spawn a git process on this machine; 0.90ms for the same query through a long-lived 'git cat-file --batch'. 24x, and process creation is the majority of a test's wall clock rather than git's work.

Git ships streaming plumbing for exactly this shape, and using it keeps full fidelity - it is still real git, the same on-disk format and the same ref semantics, so the defect classes this suite exists to catch stay catchable:
- git cat-file --batch for reads (one process, many queries)
- git hash-object --stdin-paths for blobs
- git update-index --index-info for index entries
- git fast-import where many objects or commits are written at once

Scope this tick to the read and object-write paths, held open per store instance. The commit/push batching is a separate tick because it changes what a record's durability means.
notes:
2026-09-18 11:23 - Implemented on branch work/pul-plumbing (8df53f5). Full gate 8min -> 3m26s on a quiet host, zero failures. internal/reconcile 447s -> 200s, internal/runstate 164s -> 31.6s alone, the end-to-end fixture test 18.7s -> 10.2s measured back to back.

Two changes, and the larger was not the one this tick named: /usr/bin/git on macOS is an xcrun stub (8.9ms vs 2.9ms for the binary it execs), so resolving past it once helps every invocation, in real runs as well as tests. The tick's own subject, a held-open cat-file --batch, was the smaller half.

WHERE IT STOPS, measured rather than assumed: the test still spawns 1010 git processes, which at 2.9ms is about 25-30% of its wall clock. The rest is git's actual work - fetches, pushes, tree assembly - so cutting spawn cost further cannot reach a minute. Two things were tried and rejected on measurement: core.fsync=none bought 6% (inside noise, and not worth trading local durability for), and batching rev-parse would touch only 4 call sites in this package rather than the 172 invocations a test makes.

The gate's wall clock is now internal/reconcile alone at 200s. Getting under a minute needs FEWER git operations, not cheaper ones - which is f61's structural change (one commit and one push per step instead of per record), and f61 is already blocked on this tick and already told to state the invariants before writing code.
acceptance_criteria: The store reads and writes objects through long-lived batch processes rather than one process per operation. A counted run of the same reconcile end-to-end test spawns substantially fewer git processes (report the before and after counts). Every runstate and reconcile test still passes, and the FETCH_HEAD, refmap and peek-ref guards still fail when their regressions are reintroduced.
closed_reason: Merged to main as 03a3bab (PR #2), CI green on Linux. Full gate 8min -> 3m26s, zero failures; CI's own run of the gate took 3m35s. The remaining floor is internal/reconcile at 200s and needs f61's structural change, which is recorded on the tick.
